mechanism: K=8 fused, register-delayed lazy updates. Instead of one add_lazy pass over the u64 accumulator row per pivot (8 B load + 8 B store + 4 B pivot per field op), up to 8 updates of the same accumulator are applied in one pass: acc[x] += f1*p1[x] + ... + f8*p8[x], with the partial sum held in a zmm register. The pass is split at each update's start column, so no pivot is read left of its start and the MAC count is unchanged. Three sites, each added as a new function with one dispatch line. (A) reduce_lazy_by, used by rref32_deferred forward/chunk/back: each next factor is reduce(acc[c] + sum of the pending group at c), which is the same residue the sequential path sees. (B) The B' build in reduce_pairs_fl, in a new reduce_pairs_fl_mem. (C) reduce_pairs_blocked, in a new reduce_pairs_blocked_mem: hits are sorted by (row, reducer), and each row's hits are fused 8 at a time per 256-column tile. Accumulator sums are exact integers. Normalisation runs before any flush that would take the pending updates past 256, which keeps the old bound. Stored rows are fp.reduce of identical residues, so output is bit-identical.
prediction: Written before measuring (NOTES.md): fingerprints and field_ops identical; acc words/op 0.13-0.35; modelled update bytes down 2.5-3.3x; quad_n9 150 to 105-125 ms (1.2-1.4x); cubic_n5 neutral. Outcome: the deterministic parts held (acc/op 0.131-0.142 on quad_n9, 20 to 6.2 B/op modelled). The wall-clock prediction failed for whole f4: the gain is limited to the FL phase (about 12%, indicative), because the isolated update kernel is port-bound, not bandwidth-bound, and 30-45% of quad_n9 time lies outside the dense phases.
toggle: F4_FP_MEM_OLD=1 (all sites). F4_FP_MEM_A=0 / F4_FP_MEM_B=0 / F4_FP_MEM_C=0 turn off one site each. F4_FP_MEM_STATS=1 prints per-f4-call traffic counters and phase clocks to stderr.
correctness: [pcc:unverified] Compared f4_fp_bench "3 large" against the baseline binary (HEAD a53cc497) for build 1 and build 2, default and F4_FP_MEM_OLD=1. All 13 cases are identical in basis_fp, field_ops, solve_fp, solve_field_ops, steps, max_rows and max_cols. Examples: quad_n9 5a5d7dea3744f69d / 399,396,830; quad_n8 539b2a77ccede549 / 56,664,766; cubic_n5 fbab6676a859b968 / 12,712,111; overdet_n12 3333741564c1aa21 / 84,352,865. Fingerprints are also identical across all 6 interleaved timing arms (new, old, A/A, and A0/B0/C0 with one site off). No counter changed. cargo test --release --lib f4_fp::tests: 27 passed, including the new mem_fused_apply_matches_sequential (lengths 1-257, N 1-8, clipped ranges, scalar and AVX-512) and narrow_arithmetic_matches_wide_rref. A standalone crate (mini/) holds the original kernel region verbatim; there, random rref32_deferred and FL instances (p in {31, 65521}, normalisation exercised, every site combination, F4_FP_FL_BLOCKED=0 too) give equal rows, pivots and ops. GF(2) binaries were not touched; this file is the F_p engine only.
deterministic_evidence: F4_FP_MEM_STATS=1 on quad_n9_p65521 (one f4 call). Deferred rref: 69.3M ops, accumulator words / ops 0.142, 19,077 flushes. B' build: 115.1M ops, 0.142, 37,183 flushes. Blocked pairs: 214.3M ops, 0.131, 172,412 flushes. These three sites cover 398.7M of the 399.4M field ops (99.8%). The old path touches 1.0 accumulator word per op by construction. quad_n8 ratios 0.152/0.150/0.135; overdet_n12 0.134/0.148/0.140. Largest quad_n9 step: 735 free columns, 1548 reducers, 567 pair rows, so B' is 4.4 MB, larger than the 2 MB L2. Modelled update traffic falls from 20 to 6.2 bytes per field op (3.2x).
indicative_timing: Indicative only; the host was shared with other leads' builds. Kernel in isolation (mini, 735-wide rows, min of 5), one-at-a-time vs fused-8 in ns/op: 0.149 vs 0.166 (183 KB pivot pool), 0.162 vs 0.174 (1.4 MB), 0.222 vs 0.189 (4.4 MB), 0.431 vs 0.366 (17 MB). So the plain AVX-512 kernel is port-bound (about 2.5 cycles per 8 lanes), and fusion only pays once pivots spill past L2. Phase clocks in build 2 (median of 5, quad_n9), old vs new: 1 thread f4 271.8 vs 254.3, reduce_pairs_fl 165.1 vs 145.6, rref32_deferred 31.1 vs 32.5, rest 75.6 vs 76.2 ms; 4 threads f4 199.7 vs 183.7, FL 88.2 vs 77.0, deferred 21.6 vs 19.5, rest 89.9 vs 87.2 ms. overdet_n12 at 1 thread: deferred 30.3 vs 22.9 ms. Interleaved bench at 4 threads, quad_n9: new 185.0, A/A 174.3, old 185.6 ms; the A/A spread is about 6%. quad_n8 and cubic_n5 moved in both directions within noise. A whole-f4 gain is not established.
risks: The normalisation schedule changed (normalise before a flush that would pass 256 pending updates); the bound and residues are unchanged, and tests cover it. The new unsafe AVX-512 code is const-generic N=1..8 with asserted bounds. AVX2-only hosts use a scalar fused fallback at the new sites instead of the hand-written AVX2 path. reduce_pairs_fl and reduce_pairs_blocked are copied into new _mem functions, so the f4-parallel lead's edits to the originals must be mirrored at integration. Dispatch lines sit at the top of reduce_lazy_by, reduce_pairs_fl and reduce_pairs_blocked; MemTimer guards sit in reduce_pairs_fl and rref32_deferred; mem_stats_report is called in f4(). The guards cost nothing unless F4_FP_MEM_STATS=1. The cut in bytes is real, but wall-clock may stay neutral after the serial A/A stage. Suggested next steps: a GEMM-style register-blocked C*B' microkernel (amortise B' loads and u32-to-u64 widening over 4 rows), and u16 storage of B' for p<=65521, which halves the working set to about L2.
